  WHY: This creates confusion in the logs about what unit is being measured and can lead to incorrect warnings being suppressed or false positives being raised.

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/targeted_file_context.py
  Line or code reference: lines 639-650 (read fallback after semble_overflow_budget_exhausted is set)
  Problem: When an empty clamp marks `semble_overflow_budget_exhausted = True` and `semble_fallback == "read"`, the code skips subsequent Semble queries (correct) but falls through to the read fallback at line 639. If `remaining_bytes` is 1 (the exhaustion case where max_bytes equals used_bytes + 1), line 651 reads 1 byte from the file. Later overflowing files get the marker at line 642 because `remaining_bytes` drops to 0. The first file therefore receives a 1-byte read prefix while subsequent files receive nothing, creating an asymmetry in what the model sees.
  Why it fails at runtime: In practice this requires max_bytes=1 AND semble_fallback="read" AND a Semble chunk whose first character is multi-byte. No real workflow sets max_bytes=1 (the default is 102400), and the default semble_fallback is "marker" not "read". The 1-byte read produces a truncated block with a header that says it is truncated, so no data is silently misrepresented.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 1
